questions.q: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the State falls under its: [1996]
questions.e: According to Article 131, the Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States, or between two or more States. This exclusive original jurisdiction means no other court can decide such federal disputes.

questions.q: When the Chief Justice of a High Court acts in an administrative capacity, he is subject to: [1996]
o: the writ jurisdiction of any other judges of the High Court.
special powers provided to the Chief Minister.
special control exercised by the Chief Justice of India.
discretionary powers of the Governor of the state.
questions.e: Article 226 of the Constitution empowers a High Court to issue writs. When the Chief Justice of a High Court acts in an administrative capacity, he is subject to the writ jurisdiction of any other judges of the High Court.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ No Union Territory has a High Court of its own. 2️⃣ Judges of the High Court hold office till the age of 62. [1996]
questions.e: The statement that no Union Territory has its own High Court is incorrect because the National Capital Territory of Delhi has had its own High Court since 1966. Statement 2 is correct as High Court judges hold office until the age of 62.

questions.q: According to the Constitution of India the term 'district judge' shall not include: [1996]
o: chief judge of a small cause court
questions.e: Under Article 236, the term "District Judge" includes judges of city civil courts, sessions judges, and chief judges of small cause courts, but it does not list "tribunal judge" in its definition.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Wilful disobedience or non-compliance of Court orders and use of derogatory language about judicial behaviour amount to Contempt of Court. Reason (R): Judicial activism cannot be practised without arming the judiciary with punitive powers to punish contemptuous behaviour. [1997]
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Both the assertion regarding contempt of court and the reason regarding judicial activism are true as independent statements. However, the need for punitive powers in judicial activism does not serve as the direct legal explanation for what constitutes contempt of court.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India tenders advice to the President on a matter of law or fact: [2001]
o: only if he seeks such advice
only if the issue poses a threat to the unity and integrity of the country
only if the matter relates to the Fundamental Rights of citizens
questions.e: Under Article 143 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court tenders advice to the President only if he seeks such advice on a matter of law or fact.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the High Courts in India: 1️⃣ There are eighteen High Courts in the country. 2️⃣ Three of them have jurisdiction over more than one state. [2001]
questions.e: As of the document's reporting, there are 24 High Courts in India. Six of these High Courts (Bombay, Calcutta, Guwahati, Kerala, Madras, and Punjab and Haryana) have jurisdiction over more than one state.

questions.q: The salaries and allowances of the Judges of the High Court are charged to the: [2002]
questions.e: The salaries and allowances of High Court judges are charged to the Consolidated Fund of the State. However, their pensions are payable as charged expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q: The power to enlarge the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India with respect to any matter included in the Union List of Legislative Powers rests with: [2003]
o: The Union Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs
questions.e: According to Article 138(1) of the Constitution, the Parliament has the power to enlarge the jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court with respect to any of the matters in the Union List.

questions.q: Which one of the following High Courts has the Territorial Jurisdiction over Andaman and Nicobar Islands? [2003]
questions.e: The Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands comes under the jurisdiction of the High Court of Calcutta under the Extended Jurisdiction Act of 1953.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The highest criminal court of the district is the Court of District and Session Judge. 2️⃣ The District Judge are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Courts. 3️⃣ A person to be eligible for appointment as a District Judge should be an advocate or a pleader of seven years' standing or more, or an officer in judicial service of the Union or the State. 4️⃣ When the sessions judge awards a death sentence, it must be confirmed by the High Court before it is carried out. [2004]
questions.e: These provisions are governed by Articles 233-235 regarding Subordinate Courts. The District and Sessions Judge heads the highest criminal court in a district, is appointed by the Governor, requires 7 years of legal standing, and death sentences must be confirmed by the High Court.

questions.q: According to the National Human Rights Commission Act, 1993, who amongst the following can be its Chairman? [2004]
o: Any serving Judge of the Supreme Court
Only a retired Chief Justice of a High Court
Any serving Judge of the High Court
Only a retired Chief Justice of India
questions.e: According to the NHRC Act 1993, only a retired Chief Justice of India (CJI) can be appointed as the Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in the descending order of precedence in the warrant of precedence? [2004]
o: Judges of the Supreme Court-Attorney General of India-Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha-Members of Parliament
Attorney General of India-Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha-Judges of the Supreme Court-Members of Parliament
Attorney General of India-Judges of the Supreme Court-Members of the Parliament-Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha
Judges of the Supreme Court-Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha-Attorney General of India-Members of the Parliament
questions.e: In the Indian order of precedence, Supreme Court Judges hold Rank 9, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha holds Rank 10, the Attorney General of India holds Rank 11, and Members of Parliament hold Rank 21.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ There are 25 High Courts in India. 2️⃣ Punjab, Haryana and the Union Territory of Chandigarh have a common High Court. 3️⃣ National Capital Territory of Delhi has a High Court of its own. [2005]
questions.e: While statement 1 was historically incorrect in the document (citing 24), statements 2 and 3 are correct: Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh share a High Court, and Delhi is the only Union Territory (at that time) with its own High Court.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament cannot enlarge the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India as its jurisdiction is limited to that conferred by the Constitution. 2️⃣ The officers and servants of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the concerned Chief Justice and the administrative expenses are charged on the Consolidated fund of India. [2005]
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 138(1) allows Parliament to enlarge the Supreme Court's jurisdiction regarding the Union List. Statement 2 is correct regarding the appointment of staff by the Chief Justice.

questions.q: Assertion (A): In India, every State has a High Court in its territory. Reason (R): The Constitution of India provides a High Court in each State. [2006]
o: Both 'A' and 'R' are individually true but 'R' is not the correct explanation of A'.
Both 'A' and 'R' are individually true and 'R' is the correct explanation of A'.
questions.e: Article 214 states there shall be a High Court for each State, making the Reason correct. However, the Assertion is false because several states share High Courts; for example, there are only 24 High Courts for the 29 states and 7 UTs mentioned in the text.

questions.q: Who was the Chief Justice of India when Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was introduced to the Indian judicial system? [2006]
questions.e: Justice P.N. Bhagwati was the Chief Justice of India from July 1985 to December 1986, and PIL was introduced during his tenure.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A person who has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court cannot plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except of the Supreme Court. 2️⃣ A person is not qualified for appointment as a Judge of a High Court in India unless he has for at least five years held a judicial office in the territory of India. [2006]
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because a retired High Court judge can practice in the Supreme Court and in High Courts other than the one where they held office. Statement 2 is incorrect because the qualification requires holding judicial office for at least ten years, not five.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The mode of removal of a Judge of a High Court in India is same as that of removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court. 2️⃣ After retirement from the office, a permanent judge of a High Court cannot plead or act in any court or before any authority in India. [2007]
questions.e: The procedure for removing a High Court judge is the same as that for a Supreme Court judge. Statement 2 is false as retired High Court judges can practice in the Supreme Court and other High Courts.

questions.q: How many High Courts in India have jurisdiction over more than one State (Union Territories not included)? [2008]
questions.e: Excluding Union Territories, there are 3 High Courts with jurisdiction over more than one state: Bombay (Maharashtra & Goa), Punjab and Haryana (Punjab & Haryana), and Guwahati (Assam, etc.).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Justice VR Krishna Iyer was the Chief Justice of India. 2️⃣ Justice VR Krishna Iyer is considered as one of the progenitors of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in the Indian judicial system. [2008]
questions.e: While Justice VR Krishna Iyer was a pioneer of PIL alongside Justice P.N. Bhagwati, he never served as the Chief Justice of India.

questions.q: With reference to Lok Adalats, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ An award made by a Lok Adalat is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and no appeal lies against there to any court. 2️⃣ Matrimonial/Family disputes are not covered under Lok Adalat. [2009]
questions.e: Lok Adalat awards have the force of a civil court decree and are non-appealable. Statement 2 is incorrect because Lok Adalats specifically deal with matrimonial and family disputes.

questions.q: With reference to Lok Adalats, which of the following statements is correct? [2010]
o: None of the statements given above is correct.
Lok Adalats can deal with matters which are civil and not criminal in nature.
Lok Adalats have the jurisdiction to settle matters at pre-litigating stage and not those matters pending before any court
Every Lok Adalat consists of either serving or retired judicial officers only and not any other person.
questions.e: All provided specific statements are incorrect: Lok Adalats can handle pending cases, they can deal with compoundable criminal cases, and they can include social activists or legal professionals in addition to judicial officers.

questions.q: Which of the following are included in the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court? 1️⃣ A dispute between the Government of India and one or more States 2️⃣ A dispute regarding elections to either House of the Parliament or that of Legislature of a State 3️⃣ A dispute between the Government of India and a Union Territory 4️⃣ A dispute between two or more States [2012-1]
questions.e: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131 includes disputes between the Center and states and disputes between two or more states. It does not include election disputes or disputes with Union Territories.

questions.q: With reference to the Delimitation Commission, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The orders of the Delimitation Commission cannot be challenged in a Court of Law. 2️⃣ When the orders of the Delimitation Commission are laid before the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assembly, they cannot effect any modifications in the orders. [2012-1]
questions.e: Both statements are correct: the Delimitation Commission's orders have the force of law, cannot be questioned in court, and cannot be modified by the legislatures.

questions.q: What is the provision to safeguard the autonomy of the Supreme Court of India? 1️⃣ While appointing the Supreme Court Judges, the President of India has to consult the Chief Justice of India. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court Judges can be removed by the Chief Justice of India only. 3️⃣ The salaries of the Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India to which the legislature does not have to vote. 4️⃣ All appointments of officers and staffs of the Supreme Court of India are made by the Government only after consulting the Chief Justice of India. [2012-1]
questions.e: Statement 1 and 3 are correct safeguards. Statement 2 is false because removal requires a parliamentary process, and statement 4 is false because staff are appointed by the Chief Justice, not the government.

questions.q: With reference to National Legal Services Authority, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Its objective is to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society on the basis of equal opportunity. 2️⃣ It issues guidelines for the State Legal Services Authorities to implement the legal programmes and schemes throughout the country. [2013-1]
questions.e: NALSA was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal services and organize Lok Adalats, while guiding State Authorities in implementing these schemes.

questions.q: In the context of Indian history, the Rakhmabai case of 1884 revolved around: 1️⃣ women's right to gain education 2️⃣ age of consent 3️⃣ restitution of conjugal rights [2020-1]
questions.e: The Rakhmabai case involved her refusal to live with her husband (restitution of conjugal rights), her desire to study, and eventually led to the Age of Consent Act 1891.

questions.q: In India, separation of judiciary from the executive is enjoined by [2020-1]
o: A Directive Principle of state policy
questions.e: Article 50, which is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51), prescribes the separation of the judiciary from the executive.

questions.q: No one can be compelled to sing the National Anthem since: 1️⃣ it will be violative of the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression 2️⃣ it will be violative of the Right to the Freedom of Conscience and practise and propagation of religion 3️⃣ there is no legal provision obliging anyone to sing the National Anthem [1996]
questions.e: According to the document, all three statements are correct: compelling someone to sing violates speech and religious freedom, and there is no specific legal mandate forcing the act.

questions.q: A British citizen staying in India cannot claim the right to: [1999]
o: Protection of life and personal liberty
questions.e: Rights under Article 19, including the freedom to practice any profession or trade, are available only to Indian citizens, not foreigners.

questions.q: In the Indian Constitution, the Right to Equality is granted by five Articles. They are: [2002]
questions.e: The Right to Equality is categorized under Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: Which one of the following rights was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the heart and soul of the Constitution? [2002]
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Right to Constitutional Remedies under Article 32 as the "very soul" and "very heart" of the Constitution.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 301 pertains to the Right to Property. 2️⃣ Right to Property is a legal right but not a Fundamental Right. 3️⃣ Article 300 A was inserted in the Constitutional Amendment. [2005]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false as Article 301 pertains to freedom of trade and commerce. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the 44th Amendment moved the Right to Property from Article 19 to Article 300A, making it a legal right.

questions.q: With reference to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, consider the following: 1️⃣ The Rights of Development 2️⃣ The Right to Expression 3️⃣ The Right to Recreation [2010]
questions.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) covers a full range of human rights including development, expression, and recreation.

questions.q: The Supreme Court of India tenders advice to the President of India on matters of law or fact: 1️⃣ on its own initiative (on any matter of larger public interest). 2️⃣ if he seeks such an advice. 3️⃣ only if the matters relate to the Fundamental Rights of the citizens. [2010]
questions.e: Under Article 143, the Supreme Court provides advice to the President only if he specifically seeks such advice.

questions.q: In India, if a religious sect/community is given the status of a national minority, what special advantages it is entitled to? 1️⃣ It can establish and administer exclusive educational institutions. 2️⃣ The President of India automatically nominations a representative of the community to Lok Sabha. 3️⃣ It can derive benefits from the Prime Minister's 15-Point Programme. [2011-1]
questions.e: Minorities have the right to establish educational institutions under Article 30 and can benefit from the PM's 15-Point Programme. There is no provision for automatic nomination of religious minorities to the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: India is home to lakhs of person with disabilities. What are the benefits available to them under the law? 1️⃣ Free schooling till the age of 18 years in government-run schools. 2️⃣ Preferential allotment of land for setting up business. 3️⃣ Ramps in public buildings. [2011-1]
questions.e: The PWD Act provides for free education until age 18, ramps in public buildings, and schemes for preferential allotment of land at concessional rates.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Right to education. 2️⃣ Right to equal access to public service. 3️⃣ Right to food. Which of the above is/are Human Right/Human Rights under "Universal Declaration of Human Rights"? [2011-1]
questions.e: The UDHR includes the right to education (Article 26), equal access to public service (Article 21), and a standard of living including food (Article 25).

questions.q: With reference to consumers' rights/privileges under the provisions of law in India, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ Consumers are empowered to take samples for food testing. 2️⃣ When a consumer files a complaint in any consumer forum, no fee is required to be paid. 3️⃣ In case of death of a consumer, his/her legal heir can file a complaint in the consumer forum on his/her behalf. [2012-1]
questions.e: Consumers can take food samples for testing and legal heirs can file complaints on behalf of deceased consumers. The statement regarding no fees is incorrect.

questions.q: The power of the Supreme Court of India to decide disputes between the Centre and the States falls under its [2014-1]
questions.e: Federal disputes between the Center and states fall under the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Gram Nyayalaya Act', which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ As per the Act, Gram Nyayalayas can hear only civil cases and not criminal cases. 2️⃣ The Act allows local social activists as mediators/reconciliators. [2016-1]
questions.e: Gram Nyayalayas can try both civil and criminal cases. The Act provides for a panel of social workers to act as conciliators.

questions.q: In India, Judicial Review implies [2020-1]
o: the power of the Judiciary to review its own judgements given earlier in similar or different cases.
the power of the Judiciary to question the wisdom of the laws enacted by the Legislatures.
the power of the Judiciary to pronounce upon the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
the power of the Judiciary to review all the legislative enactments before they are assented to by the President.
questions.e: Judicial review is the power of the Supreme Court or High Courts to examine the constitutionality of any law or executive order.

questions.q: "Rule of Law Index" is released by which of the following? [2018-1]
o: The Office of UN Commissioner for Human Rights
questions.e: The Rule of Law Index is released by the World Justice Project.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As per the Right to Education (RTE) Act, to be eligible for appointment as a teacher in a State, a person would be required to possess the minimum qualification laid down by the concerned State Council of Teacher Education. 2️⃣ As per the RTE Act, for teaching primary classes, a candidate is required to pass a Teacher Eligibility Test conducted in accordance with the National Council of Teacher Education guidelines. 3️⃣ In India, more than 90% of teacher's education institutions are directly under the State Governments. [2018-1]
questions.e: Under the RTE Act, the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), not state councils, sets minimum qualifications. Clearing the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is a mandatory requirement for appointment.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ As per recent amendment to the India Forest Act, 1927, forest dwellers have the right to fell the bamboos grown on the forest areas. 2️⃣ As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, bamboo is a minor forest produce. 3️⃣ The Scheduled Tribes and other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 allows ownership of minor forest produce to forest dwellers. [2019-1]
questions.e: The amendment to the Indian Forest Act removed "bamboos" grown on non-forest areas from the definition of trees to allow farmers to fell them. The Forest Rights Act of 2006 classifies bamboo as minor forest produce and allows forest dwellers ownership of such produce.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India safeguards one's right to marry the person of one's choice? [2019-1]
questions.e: The Supreme Court, in the Hadiya case judgement, ruled that the right to marry a person of one's choice is integral to the right to life and liberty under Article 21.

questions.q: Which one of the following categories of Fundamental Rights incorporates protection against untouchability as a form of discrimination? [2020-1]
questions.e: Article 17, which provides for the abolition of untouchability, is categorized under the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).

questions.q: In India, Legal Services Authorities provide free legal services to which of the following type of citizens? 1️⃣ Person with an annual income of less than Rs. 1,00,000 2️⃣ Transgender with an annual income of less than Rs. 2,00,000 3️⃣ Member of Other Backward Classes (OBC) with an annual income of less than Rs. 3,00,000 4️⃣ All Senior Citizens [2020-1]
questions.e: Free legal aid is provided based on income criteria for specific groups; however, there is no provision specifically for OBCs under the Legal Services Authority Act. Not all senior citizens are eligible; their eligibility depends on income limits.
